facts.fact: The page states that 86% of all Google Business Profile views come from discovery searches (like 'dresses near me') rather than from people searching for the specific brand, a figure the vendor presents without naming a source.
facts.quote: A staggering **86% of all GBP views** come from discovery searches (like "dresses near me"), not from people searching for your specific brand.

facts.fact: The page says its chart of benefits from a fully detailed Google Business Profile is based on 2026 performance data, but the chart's values are not given in the text.
facts.quote: Here is a quick look at the tangible benefits you can expect from a fully detailed GBP, based on 2026 performance data.

facts.fact: Google Business Profile product and service descriptions can be up to 1,000 characters long, according to the Adwave article.
facts.quote: You get up to **1,000 characters**, but you don't need to use them all.

facts.fact: Adwave states that for service-based businesses, clicks-to-call can account for 10% to 15% of all profile views.
facts.quote: for service-based businesses, clicks-to-call can account for **10% to 15% of all profile views**.

facts.fact: Adwave estimates that a 10% to 15% clicks-to-call share could translate to around 50 phone calls every month, a figure presented as an illustrative estimate.
facts.quote: That could easily translate to around 50 phone calls every month.

facts.fact: In its example, Adwave suggests setting the price for an AI-Powered TV Advertising service to 'From $30 a day'.
facts.quote: you could set the price to "**From $30 a day**."

facts.fact: Adwave states that profiles with a solid photo library often see a 30% to 50% bump in engagement.
facts.quote: profiles with a solid photo library often see a **30% to 50% bump in engagement**.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends product photos at least 1200px by 900px in resolution.
facts.quote: Aim for photos that are at least 1200px by 900px.

facts.fact: Adwave cites that 46% of all Google queries are for local information.
facts.quote: **46% of all Google queries** are for local information.

facts.fact: Citing RightChoice.ai, Adwave reports that 59% of consumers use Google to research a purchase they plan to make in-store or locally.
facts.quote: **59% of consumers** using Google to research a purchase they plan to make in-store or locally

facts.fact: Google Business Profile product listings get a call-to-action button, and the page lists three options: Order Online / Buy, Learn More, and Get Offer.
facts.quote: Every product listing gets a call-to-action (CTA) button, and this small detail is important.

facts.fact: According to Adwave's guidance, new Google Business Profile products or services usually appear on the public profile within a few minutes after being added.
facts.quote: You can often add a new product or service and see it live on your public profile in just a few minutes.

facts.fact: Adwave advises that if a new Google Business Profile item has not appeared after one hour, the owner should wait up to 24 hours before taking further action, since every item goes through an automated Google policy review.

Google's automated review of added products or services checks compliance with its policies, and Adwave says items still missing after one day should be checked for policy notifications or resubmitted.
facts.quote: If it's still missing after a day, pop into your GBP dashboard to check for any policy notifications or try submitting it again.

facts.fact: Google may reject a product listing whose title contains promotional text, such as a discount percentage like '50% OFF' or a phrase like 'Best Deal in Town'.
facts.quote: Titles like "**50% OFF** Summer Sale" or "Best Deal in Town" are a no-go.

facts.fact: Google may reject a product listing that lists a service as a product, such as 'Free Consultation' in the Products tab.
facts.quote: **Listing a service as a product:** You can't put "Free Consultation" in your Products tab.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends reviewing the entire Google Business Profile product and service list at least once a quarter.
facts.quote: it's a great habit to review your entire product and service list at least once a quarter

facts.fact: Adwave advises updating a Google Business Profile when a service is added, a price changes, or an unavailable product is removed.
facts.quote: Update your Google Business Profile when you add a service, change a price, or remove an unavailable product.
